body:
I can reproduce the issue just by adding the `capsule_184x69.jpg` file to a Godot project, it fails importing.

I can confirm @DanielKinsman's comment that the same version of libjpeg-turbo which we're using (3.1.3) can decode it fine (built the library from source in the `3.1.3` tag and decompressed with `./djpeg -verbose -outfile out.pnm capsule_184x69.jpg`).

Round-tripping the file through PNG to get a "standard" JPG from ImageMagick's default settings, I get a smaller JPG that works fine in Godot:
```
$ ls -l capsule_*
-rw-r--r--. 1 akien akien 585533 Jan 31 13:34 capsule_184x69.jpg
-rw-r--r--. 1 akien akien  28441 Jan 31 13:47 capsule_184x69.png
-rw-r--r--. 1 akien akien  24287 Jan 31 13:48 capsule_184x69.png.jpg
$ file capsule_*
capsule_184x69.jpg:     JPEG image data, JFIF standard 1.01, resolution (DPI), density 300x300, segment length 16, Exif Standard: [TIFF image data, big-endian, direntries=7, orientation=upper-left, xresolution=98, yresolution=106, resolutionunit=2, software=Adobe Photoshop CS6 (Windows), datetime=2016:11:09 17:15:48], baseline, precision 8, 184x69, components 4
capsule_184x69.png:     PNG image data, 184 x 69, 8-bit/color RGB, non-interlaced
capsule_184x69.png.jpg: JPEG image data, JFIF standard 1.01, resolution (DPI), density 300x300, segment length 16, Exif Standard: [TIFF image data, big-endian, direntries=7, orientation=upper-left, xresolution=98, yresolution=106, resolutionunit=2, software=Adobe Photoshop CS6 (Windows), datetime=2016:11:09 17:15:48], baseline, precision 8, 184x69, components 3
```

So the difference between the original file (`capsule_184x69.jpg`) and the one converted to PNG and then back to JPG with ImageMagick (`capsule_184x69.png.jpg`) seems to lie in the number of components (4 vs 3).

I'm not very familiar with the JPEG format so I'm not sure what's in this component and why it's ~550 KB, but that seems to be a clue. Maybe we don't implement 4-components support in Godot.

The problem is that the file uses CMYK colorspace (intended for printing) and we don't support it currently. The code we have tries to force decompressing it as RGB8 which doesn't make sense.

#115674 should make this lack of support explicit.

I'm not super familiar with turbojpeg so I've tried to vibe code a fix with ChatGPT and it kept hallucinating APIs until it admitteed (possibly still making it up) that TurboJPEG explicitly doesn't support converting CMYK to RGB.

In fact it seems like TurboJPEG does have some minimal support for it, but it's called a hack: 
```
 * @param pixelFormat pixel format of the packed-pixel image (see @ref TJPF
 * "Pixel formats".)  If this parameter is set to @ref TJPF_GRAY, then the
 * image will be stored in PGM or 8-bit-per-pixel (indexed color) BMP format.
 * Otherwise, the image will be stored in PPM or 24-bit-per-pixel BMP format.
 * If this parameter is set to @ref TJPF_CMYK, then the CMYK pixels will be
 * converted to RGB using a quick & dirty algorithm that is suitable only for
 * testing purposes.  (Proper conversion between CMYK and other formats
 * requires a color management system.)
 *
 * @return 0 if successful, or -1 if an error occurred (see #tj3GetErrorStr().)
 */
DLLEXPORT int tj3SaveImage8(tjhandle handle, const char *filename,
                            const unsigned char *buffer, int width, int pitch,
                            int height, int pixelFormat);
```

@DanielKinsman Note that `djpeg` is actually using the standard libjpeg API, not TurboJPEG. `tjdecomp` can be used instead to test the TurboJPEG API (and it uses `tj3SaveImage8` with the above mention). From a quick look, its code in `cmyk.h` (clearly labelled only for testing) seems to be used only when outputting to PNM.

Allegedly we may be able to fallback to libjpeg to do the proper conversion.

> From a quick look, its code in `cmyk.h` (clearly labelled only for testing) seems to be used only when outputting to PNM.

I had a go at implementing ad hoc conversion with this helper method, and it seems to work ok in early tests: #115688.
